title: Independence of cycle-space basis-matrix columns and bonds
statement: Let $V$ and $A$ be finite sets of vertices and arcs, let each arc $a\in A$ have a tail $\mathrm{tail}(a)\in V$ and a head $\mathrm{head}(a)\in V$, and let $F$ be a field, so that the cycle space $\mathcal{C}\le (A\to F)$ is defined. Let $C$ be a basis matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ — a matrix whose rows form a basis of $\mathcal{C}$ — and let $S\subseteq A$ be a finite set of arcs. Then the columns of the restriction $C\mid S$ (the submatrix of $C$ keeping exactly the columns labelled by elements of $S$) are linearly independent over $F$ if and only if $S$ contains no bond, that is, there is no bond $B$ with $B\subseteq S$.
hypotheses_covered: V, A finite sets of vertices and arcs with tail/head maps
C is a basis matrix of the cycle space (rows form a basis)
S is a finite subset of arcs
columns of C restricted to S are linearly independent
iff no bond B is contained in S
